headline: Flames’ Mikael Backlund day-to-day with upper-body injury
take:
Mikael Backlund is day-to-day with an upper-body injury after leaving Sunday's game against the Carolina Hurricanes and not returning, Daily Faceoff reports. The Flames have not been given a timeline in the report.

That matters for a CGY team already struggling at 2-6-0. Backlund has been a steadying presence so far this season: at 5-on-5, CGY has controlled 52.29% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) when he is on the ice, well above the team's 48% overall, and the team's share runs 4.88 percentage points better with him in the lineup. His own two points on 2.87 expected goals suggest his scoring has lagged his chances (goals minus expected is -1.87), so he is a modest bounce-back candidate once healthy, though the sample is only eight games. He also averages 17.73 minutes a night, kills penalties and sits on the first line, so his absence would be felt in several spots.

If he misses time, the minutes would likely go to Joel Farabee, who plays 19:16 a night. That is a projection based on how the coach has used his players, not on games already played without Backlund.
